stem:
A 30-year-old woman from a region without iodized salt presents with an enlarged thyroid. Her follicle cells still produce their usual storage protein, but hormone output is low because a critical element is missing.

In the normal gland, thyroxine (T4) is assembled when iodine is first linked to which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Tryptophan residues within the follicle cell cytosol
options.misconception: The wrong amino acid substrate is being chosen for thyroid hormone.
options.explanation: Amine hormones from tryptophan include melatonin; thyroid hormones are built by iodinating the tyrosines of thyroglobulin within the follicle colloid.

options.label: B
options.text: Free thyroid hormone already circulating in the blood
options.misconception: A downstream product is being named as the synthetic substrate.
options.explanation: T3 and T4 are synthesized in the colloid by iodinating thyroglobulin tyrosines, then stored until TSH triggers their release; circulating hormone is the endpoint, not the substrate.

options.label: C
options.text: Tyrosine residues within thyroglobulin in the colloid
options.misconception: None; peroxidase enzymes iodinate thyroglobulin's tyrosines, and coupled intermediaries form T3 and T4.
options.explanation: In the colloid, peroxidase links iodine to tyrosine amino acids in thyroglobulin; one- and two-iodine intermediaries then couple to form T3, and two two-iodine intermediaries form T4.

options.label: D
options.text: Cholesterol side chains in the follicle cell membrane
options.misconception: The steroid hormone precursor is being applied to an amino acid-derived hormone.
options.explanation: Steroid hormones derive from cholesterol; T3 and T4 are amino acid-derived hormones assembled by iodinating tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin in the colloid.

options.label: E
options.text: Calcitonin precursors in the parafollicular cells
options.misconception: The thyroid's other secretory cell type is being confused with follicle cell synthesis.
options.explanation: Parafollicular cells secrete calcitonin for calcium homeostasis; T3 and T4 come from iodinated thyroglobulin tyrosines within follicle colloid.

context: Learning objective: outline T3/T4 synthesis and release. Peroxidase links iodine to thyroglobulin tyrosines in the colloid; coupled intermediaries yield T3/T4, stored in colloid until TSH stimulates endocytosis and lysosomal release into blood. Dietary iodine deficiency blocks synthesis and causes goiter.
imageCaption: Thyroid synthesis: NIS iodide uptake; TPO iodinates thyroglobulin tyrosines; couple to T3/T4.
